requirements.source_quote: Requests to /work pass through the checks in this order: load shedding, then rate limiting, then the circuit breaker, then the backend.
requirements.summary: Protection chain order is shed, rate-limit, breaker, backend
requirements.untestable_reason: Order is only observable black-box when two checks would reject the same request at the same moment; not reliably reproducible against a live service. Belongs in an in-process middleware test.

requirements.source_quote: When 50 requests are already in flight, additional requests are rejected immediately with 503 and body "server overloaded, try again shortly".
requirements.summary: Over 50 in-flight requests are shed with 503 and a specific body
Shed requests are rejected without waiting

requirements.source_quote: Each client is limited to 5 requests per second sustained, with a burst of 20.
requirements.summary: Token bucket: 5 req/s sustained, burst 20, per client

requirements.source_quote: A client is identified by the Fly-Client-IP header when present, otherwise by the IP address of the connection, ignoring the port.
requirements.summary: Client identity is Fly-Client-IP, else connection IP without port

requirements.source_quote: Over-limit requests are rejected with 429, body "rate limit exceeded", and a Retry-After header of at least 1 second.
requirements.summary: 429 response shape: body text and Retry-After >= 1

requirements.source_quote: After 5 backend failures the breaker opens.
While open, requests are rejected with 503 and body "backend unavailable".
requirements.summary: Open breaker rejects with 503 backend unavailable

requirements.source_quote: After a 10 second cooldown the breaker allows a trial request; success closes it, failure reopens it.
/metrics reports flowgate_requests_total with an outcome label (allowed, error, shed, rate_limited, breaker_open), flowgate_breaker_state, and flowgate_in_flight_requests.
requirements.summary: Metrics endpoint exposes the three named series

requirements.source_quote: p95 latency of /work at or below 150 ms under about 2,000 requests per second sustained.
Backend success rate of at least 95% for admitted requests.

open_questions.question: Does "after 5 backend failures" mean 5 consecutive failures or 5 within a time window? BREAKER_THRESHOLD makes the breaker drivable, but the PRD does not say which counting rule it uses, so a test at the documented threshold of 5 cannot assert the boundary.
Fly-Client-IP is trusted from any caller. Off Fly's edge, a client can rotate that header to bypass rate limiting. Is the gateway guaranteed to only ever run behind Fly's edge?
The live deployment runs more than one instance with per-instance state. Should rate-limit and metrics tests run against a single pinned instance?

The 2026-09-11 SLO numbers were measured while every connection counted as a new client. With per-IP limiting fixed, how will load be generated from enough client identities to reproduce ~2,000 req/s?

out_of_scope: Fly.io deployment configuration and CI workflow
